steps.title: Add a facade
steps.caption: Put a routing facade in front of the monolith. At first, every route still goes to legacy.
steps.body: Place a **facade** (an API gateway, reverse proxy or routing layer) in front of the legacy system. Clients now talk to the facade, which forwards every route to the monolith unchanged. Nothing has migrated yet, but you now control where each request goes.

steps.title: Extract /catalog
steps.caption: Rebuild /catalog as a new service and flip its route. The old catalog module goes dark.
steps.body: Pick one capability with clear boundaries, rebuild it as a new service, and **flip its route** in the facade. The matching code in the monolith stops receiving traffic and can be deleted later.

steps.title: Peel off more
steps.caption: Keep peeling: /orders and /users move over one at a time. Rolling back is just a route flip.
steps.body: Repeat, one route at a time, in whatever order delivers value or reduces risk. Each step is small and reversible: if the new service misbehaves, flip the route back to legacy.

steps.title: Retire the monolith
steps.caption: The last route moves. With no traffic left, the monolith is decommissioned.
steps.body: When the last route has moved, the monolith serves nothing and can be switched off. The new system has grown around the old one and replaced it, like the strangler fig vine the pattern is named after.
